title: Review of c52's predator-turnover swings: labkit re-runs of the neutral arm on fresh seeds 6 and 7 reproduce one full prey swing with a second trough, trough spacing ~6600 and ~7800 t
summary: Labkit runs of world2g.py with the neutral-arm parameters (yg 0.5, kdec 5e-4, mconv 1e-3, both kinds hunting), 128^2, t=16000, seeds 6 and 7. Prey bodies (c_a > 0.5, area >= 4) every 1000 t from t=2000: seed 6 39, 16, 7, 5, 6, 6, 20, 25, 26, 15, 4, 8, 10, 20, 20; seed 7 44, 10, 6, 5, 9, 11, 21, 24, 19, 15, 9, 7, 12, 14, 22. Smoothed (900 t window) troughs at t=4900-6600 and 12300 (seed 6), 4800-6500 and 13400 (seed 7); peaks at 9700 and 8900; predator bodies (b + e) peak at t~9500-10000, after the prey, and fall to 16-18 at the prey trough. labkit: 0 persistent tracks or splits for any kind at K=20 (bodies turn over).

observations.X: cycles_rerun.png, cycles_rerun.json: on both fresh seeds the prey fall from ~40 to ~5 by t~5000, recover to 25-29 at t~9000-9700 with the predators following, fall again to 4-7 at t=12300 / 13400, and rise to 20-22 by t=16000; trough-to-trough spacing ~6600 (seed 6, from the middle of the broad first trough) and ~7800 (seed 7), in the 7000-7700 range reported

seeds_run.result: pass: two prey troughs, one peak between, second rise

verdicts.limitation: Two troughs per run, as in the finding: a spacing, not a period distribution. The first trough is broad (t~4800-6600), so its time depends on the smoothing. Predator lag behind prey is short (~300-800 t between peaks). No selective arm, no grid check of my own; labkit finds no persistent tracks or splits at K=20 for any kind in this variant, so the swings are population turnover, not lineages.
